children: , the custom-chip and networking supplier, warned that funding could become the biggest obstacle to AI expansion, according to Reuters, as shares traded at $356.60, down approximately 1.4% at 10.50am EST. CEO Hock Tan's message puts customers' spending capacity squarely in focus. Demand for more computing power still needs someone to pay the bill.

The stakes are already enormous. Broadcom reported fiscal-third-quarter AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion, up 221% from a year earlier. That accounted for roughly 56.4% of its $29.6 billion total revenue. AI now supplies more than half the sales engine, making customers' ability to finance their next buildout a central investment question.

The valuation snapshot places the shares 16.08% below the $424.92 GF Value estimate, suggesting potential upside if Broadcom delivers, though that estimate offers no guarantee. The risk is timing. Custom accelerators need buildings, electricity and networking before they can earn their keep. If financing gets harder or projected returns disappoint, customers could delay projects even while their appetite for chips remains strong. For investors, the question is how quickly that appetite turns into funded orders.

title: Broadcom Stocks Fall 1.4% as Hock Tan Calls Capital AI's Bottleneck
